CheckTitle: Conditional Access ensures user risk and sign-in risk are enforced in separate policies
Description:
Conditional Access policies that set both **user risk** and **sign-in risk** conditions combine them with AND logic, so the policy only applies when both risks are present simultaneously.

This leaves most risk events uncovered. Microsoft recommends creating **separate policies** for user risk and sign-in risk to ensure each risk type is independently enforced.
Risk:
A policy that combines user risk and sign-in risk only triggers when **both** conditions are true at the same time. A compromised user signing in without a risky sign-in, or a risky sign-in from a low-risk user, bypasses the policy entirely.

Administrators may believe Identity Protection is enforced while most risk events remain unmitigated.

Code.Other:
1. Navigate to the **Microsoft Entra admin center** at https://entra.microsoft.com/
2. Go to **Protection** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**
3. Select the policy that combines both risk conditions
4. Under **Conditions**, remove one of the risk conditions (keep only **User risk** or only **Sign-in risk**)
5. Create a **new policy** for the removed risk type using the recommended templates: *Require password change for high-risk users* or *Require MFA for elevated sign-in risk*
6. Validate in **Report-only** mode, then switch to **On**

Recommendation.Text: Configure **separate Conditional Access policies** for user risk and sign-in risk. Because all conditions in a policy are ANDed, combining both risk types in one policy creates a gap where individual risk events are not covered. Use Microsoft's risk-based policy templates to ensure each risk type is independently enforced.

Notes: Inspired by Maester control MT.1049. Report-only policies are also evaluated because they are misconfigured and will be ineffective once enforced. Requires Entra ID P2 for risk conditions.
